questions.prompt: Which statement best matches the ISTQB view of testing?
options: Only running the software to find bugs
A set of activities, static and dynamic, to find defects and evaluate quality
questions.explanation: Testing includes planning, analysis, design, implementation, execution and completion.

questions.prompt: Reviewing a requirements document for ambiguities counts as testing.
questions.explanation: Static testing is part of testing.

options: Finding and fixing the cause of a failure
questions.explanation: Testing finds failures; debugging finds and fixes causes.

questions.prompt: A tester reports checkout fails with exactly 100 items. A developer reproduces it, finds a loop limit set to 99 and corrects it. The tester re-runs the failed test. Which was debugging?
options: The developer's finding and correcting the loop limit
questions.explanation: Debugging is the developer's analysis and fix. The re-run is confirmation testing.

questions.prompt: Which are test activities in the ISTQB test process? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Along with monitoring and control throughout, these form the process.

questions.prompt: Why does testing provide value even when it finds nothing wrong?
options: It gives stakeholders information, confidence and evidence for decisions
questions.explanation: Information for decisions is a key objective.

questions.prompt: A manager says 'testing is just clicking around at the end'. Which correction is best?
options: Testing starts early (reviews, planning, design) and includes analysis, design, execution and reporting, not just running at the end
questions.explanation: Testing is a process throughout the lifecycle.

questions.prompt: A developer says 'my unit tests passed so nobody needs to test'. Best answer?
options: Unit tests are one level; other levels and perspectives find defects units cannot, and test independence reduces bias
questions.explanation: Different levels and viewpoints find different defects.

questions.prompt: A failure is observed in production. Which sequence describes the relationship correctly?
options: Failure, then defect, then error, found by debugging
A person makes an error, creating a defect in the work product; executing it can cause a failure that testing observes; debugging finds the defect
A defect always causes a failure
questions.explanation: Errors cause defects; defects may cause failures if executed.
